textbookText: Some of its characteristic features are listed below: i. They were similar to modern men in terms of size and appearance. ii. Their faces had jaws that were not projected forward. iii. They had moderate brow ridges, strong jaws and dentition like man, and a welldeveloped chin. iv. They were around 5 feet tall with broad forehead and raised narrow nose and prominent chin. v. They could walk and run faster. vi. They were cave dwellers and had left a few beautiful murals of animals on the cave's wall. vii. They used to live in families and were good at making tools and even ornaments, not only of stones and bones, but also of elephant tusks. Its tools included spears, bows and arrows. viii. Their cranial capacity was 1600 c.c. which is more than modern man. Thus, it was believed that they were more intelligent and cultured than the man of today. ix. They were unaware of agriculture, domestication and socialization by then.

8. The Living Modern Man (Homo sapiens sapiens) Further evolution of man after Cro-Magnon was of culture rather than of anatomy. During the ice age between 75,000-10,000 years ago modern H. sapiens appeared in the region around Caspean and Mediterranean seas. Then, they spread all over the world to become a dominating species. Around 18,000 years ago prehistoric cave art developed, one of which can be observed at Bhimbetka rock shelter in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, India. H. sapiens sapiens appeared in the Holocene epoch. Their lifestyle evolved from cave dwelling and hunting type to crop raising type in around 10,000 years with which human settlements started. Morphologically, they were similar to modern man in all aspect however following morphological evolution are distinctly observed in modern man: i. Modern men have slight raises in the skull cap. ii. Their skull bones are thinner. iii. There is slight reduction in cranial capacity which is about 1450 cc. iv. They developed four curves in the vertebral column.
